style.interpretation: Model-authored art direction from the complete 110-room source inventory; creative choices are artistic, not canonical.

target.crop: Safe center crop from 4:3 to 256:159; protect subjects within the central 82.8% of source height and central 90% of width.

style.style: Painterly adventure-game illustration recalling fine late-1980s and early-1990s computer artwork; natural proportions, restrained brushwork, readable silhouettes and broad tonal masses.
style.architecture: Domestic white-painted colonial timberwork; underground construction uses broad fitted stone and worn timber where source establishes buildings. Industrial dam and mine structures use sober utilitarian forms. Egyptian tomb vocabulary only in the named tomb. Do not add columns, arches or machinery merely to decorate a cave.
style.landscape: A coherent temperate forest of pines and hemlocks, open fields, pale river cliffs and distant severe mountains. Use the plant types only where compatible with extracted descriptions; do not add a mountain or forest to enclosed rooms.
style.geology: Rock masses are simplified into legible planes; retain explicit granite, sand, white cliffs and mud separately. Generic cave rock receives subdued earth and slate tones as an artistic material choice.
style.lighting: Exterior default is quiet midmorning daylight, upper-left in each local frame, with soft haze only in distant open views. Forest interiors receive filtered light. Enclosed underground views use dim, non-diegetic illustrative fill with deep edge shadows; never invent a visible lamp, sunbeam, window or magical glow as its source. Explicit story light or darkness takes precedence.
style.palette: Aim for roughly 256 visually significant colors, broad related color regions, controlled shading and clear dark/light separation. No exact RGB-count requirement, photographic color noise, excessive gradients or microtextures.
style.perspective: Human-scale viewpoints with believable perspective. Choose framing per room; keep each room camera, static geometry, palette and lighting fixed across states.
style.atmosphere: Evocative, quiet and slightly uncanny; readable foreground and midground, restrained atmospheric perspective only when spatial depth supports it.
exclusions: No artificial pixel grid or enlarged pixel effects
No UI, border, caption, lettering or readable text
No invented characters, significant objects, exits or events
No color quantization, image generation or YJK conversion in this phase
assumptions: Daylight timing, illumination direction, unspecified material finish and camera design are artistic choices.
Illustrative fill is a visibility convention, not an in-world light fixture.
A blank inscription surface preserves its physical carrier while honoring the no-text brief; wording remains in canonical provenance.

groups.canonical: One white house, boarded front door, boarded north/south windows, a small rear kitchen window; interiors connected by the extracted exits.
groups.artistic: Modest colonial timber dwelling, simple pitched roof, weathered white painted boards; do not introduce extra doors or windows. Pale plaster and dark brown timber inside. Keep roof pitch, wall finish, trim proportions and window construction across views.
groups.inferred: The kitchen east window is the rear window viewed from behind the house; maintain the same frame and sill in both views.

groups.canonical: Temperate forest, the path tree with low branches, and source-marked clearings and mountain barriers.
groups.artistic: Deep green pine/hemlock masses and warm muted soil. Preserve the path tree trunk and lowest bough shapes between ground and branch views.
groups.inferred: Connected forest locations belong to the same landscape; do not imply unrecorded direct sightlines.

groups.canonical: Frigid River, pale White Cliffs, dam, the 450-foot Aragain Falls and the source-directed rainbow span.
groups.artistic: Pale warm cliffs in large horizontal rock masses, dark teal water, chalk-white foam and restrained blue-gray mist; one consistent gorge and falls silhouette.
groups.inferred: Use river adjacency for geological continuity, not permission to show the dam from every river view.

groups.canonical: Flood-control dam, water-level variants, control panel and maintenance facilities.
groups.artistic: Massive plain concrete engineering, dark iron fittings, restrained green/red/blue/yellow controls; lock bank contours and dam silhouette across water states.
groups.inferred: Use connected waterways to unify wet rock color; sound alone does not authorize visible turbulence in a different room.

groups.canonical: Dome, wood railing, marble pedestal, temple and source-established tomb/gateway features.
groups.artistic: Broad worn stone planes, ivory marble where explicit, dark brown timber; restrained ceremonial scale without adding religious symbols.
groups.inferred: Dome upper railing and lower pedestal must share vertical geometry across the two room views.

groups.canonical: Coal workings, shaft chain/basket, wood ladder, loose timber and machine where described.
groups.artistic: Charcoal and umber with broad worn wood planes; reserve shiny metal for explicit fittings.
groups.inferred: Shaft and ladder views show opposite ends of the same structures, preserving chain thickness and rung spacing.

groups.canonical: Small twisty passages described as all alike; skeleton only where established.
groups.artistic: Consistent tight gray-brown passage treatment. Do not add marks, numbers, different colored doors or other navigation clues. Each room retains its own asset even if prompts are similar.
groups.inferred: Shared treatment follows the repeated source description; no new map topology is implied.

groups.canonical: Two large square tall rooms, each with a south-wall mirror and exits on the other three sides.
groups.artistic: Same mirror border proportions and cool neutral stone finish. Reflect only established geometry; no player portrait or extra passage.
groups.inferred: Treat them as a visual pair while preserving distinct room and state identities.

groups.canonical: Use the explicit room geometry, granite, dampness and construction facts from each room.
groups.artistic: Broad cool gray and brown stone planes and soft non-diegetic illustrative fill. Do not add common fixtures to unrelated rooms.
groups.inferred: Shared palette suggests an underground world; it asserts no extra passage connections.
